question: A company wants a foundation model to answer customer questions using its own internal product documentation without retraining the model. Which approach best fits this need?
options: Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG)
Continued pre-training
Full fine-tuning
Reinforcement learning from human feedback
explanation: RAG retrieves relevant content from an external knowledge source at inference time and supplies it to the model, allowing answers grounded in private documents without changing the model's weights.

question: Which metric is most commonly used to evaluate the quality of machine-generated text summaries by comparing them to reference summaries?
options: ROUGE
F1 score for tabular classification
Mean absolute error
R-squared
explanation: ROUGE measures the overlap of n-grams between generated and reference text and is widely used to evaluate summarization quality.

question: What does the BLEU metric primarily assess?
options: The quality of machine-translated or generated text against reference text
The latency of a model's inference responses
The total cost of running an inference workload
The diversity of a training dataset
explanation: BLEU (Bilingual Evaluation Understudy) compares machine-generated text to one or more reference texts and is commonly used to evaluate translation and generation quality.

question: Which Amazon Bedrock feature helps block harmful content and filter undesirable topics in foundation model inputs and outputs?
options: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails
Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases
Amazon Bedrock Agents
Amazon Bedrock Provisioned Throughput
explanation: Guardrails for Amazon Bedrock lets you define content filters, denied topics, and word filters to safeguard model inputs and outputs.

question: A team wants to evaluate whether a chatbot's tone and helpfulness meet expectations in ways that are hard to measure automatically. Which evaluation method is most appropriate?
options: Human evaluation
BLEU scoring only
Token counting
Measuring GPU utilization
explanation: Human evaluation uses people to judge subjective qualities like tone, helpfulness, and relevance that automated metrics often cannot fully capture.

question: What is the main purpose of using a benchmark dataset when evaluating a foundation model?
options: To provide a standardized set of inputs and expected outputs for consistent comparison
To reduce the model's parameter count
To encrypt the model weights
To increase the model's context window
explanation: Benchmark datasets offer a standardized, repeatable way to measure and compare model performance across tasks.

question: Which of the following is a business KPI that could be used to evaluate the real-world success of a generative AI customer-support assistant?
options: Average customer handling time reduction
Number of layers in the neural network
Size of the model checkpoint in gigabytes
Number of attention heads
explanation: Business KPIs such as reduced handling time, higher customer satisfaction, or deflection rate measure the practical value the model delivers.

question: Fine-tuning a foundation model requires which of the following?
options: A labeled dataset of examples for the target task
Only a single prompt at inference time
Disabling all model weights
A vector database of unlabeled documents
explanation: Fine-tuning adjusts a model's weights using a labeled dataset of task-specific examples to improve performance on that task.

question: Which Amazon Bedrock capability lets you compare multiple foundation models using automatic or human-based evaluations before choosing one?
options: Amazon Bedrock model evaluation
Amazon Bedrock Marketplace billing
Amazon Bedrock Guardrails
Amazon Bedrock fine-tuning jobs
explanation: Amazon Bedrock provides model evaluation jobs that support automatic and human evaluation to help select the best model for a use case.

question: When choosing a foundation model, which factor relates to how quickly the model returns a response to a user?
options: Latency
Number of training epochs
Vocabulary embedding size
Dataset license
explanation: Latency measures the time it takes for a model to produce a response, an important trade-off in interactive applications.

question: Which statement best describes RAG compared to fine-tuning?
options: RAG supplies external knowledge at inference time, while fine-tuning changes the model's weights
RAG always changes the model's weights, while fine-tuning never does
RAG and fine-tuning are identical techniques
RAG requires more labeled training data than fine-tuning
explanation: RAG augments prompts with retrieved context without modifying weights, whereas fine-tuning updates the model's parameters with training data.

question: Why might a smaller foundation model be preferred over a larger one for a high-volume, simple classification task?
options: Lower cost and lower latency
It always produces more creative text
It has a larger context window
It requires no input data
explanation: Smaller models typically cost less per inference and respond faster, which can be ideal for simple, high-volume tasks where a large model is unnecessary.

question: A company has a large corpus of unlabeled industry-specific documents and wants the model to better understand domain vocabulary and patterns broadly. Which customization approach is most appropriate?
options: Continued pre-training
Retrieval Augmented Generation
Prompt engineering only
Guardrails configuration
explanation: Continued pre-training uses large amounts of unlabeled domain data to adapt a model's general knowledge to a specific domain.

question: A team needs a model that responds in a very specific brand voice and consistently follows a structured output format for a narrow task. They have thousands of labeled example pairs. Which approach fits best?
options: Fine-tuning
RAG with a vector store
Increasing the temperature parameter
Continued pre-training on unlabeled web data
explanation: Fine-tuning on labeled input-output pairs is well suited for teaching a model a consistent style, tone, and output format for a specific task.

question: Which scenario is the strongest reason to choose RAG over fine-tuning?
options: The knowledge changes frequently and must stay current without retraining
The model must permanently learn a new writing style
There is a large labeled dataset of question-answer pairs
The goal is to reduce the model's parameter count
explanation: RAG is ideal when information changes often, because updating the knowledge source keeps responses current without the cost of retraining.

question: Which practices are part of good data preparation before fine-tuning a foundation model on Amazon Bedrock? (Select TWO.)
options: Ensuring the data is clean, well-formatted, and representative of the task
Removing personally identifiable information that should not be in the model
Maximizing the number of duplicate and irrelevant examples
Setting the inference temperature to its highest value
Disabling all evaluation after training
explanation: Good data preparation includes using clean, representative, well-formatted data and removing sensitive information, since the fine-tuned model learns directly from this data.

question: An application sends very long prompts with large retrieved contexts on every request. Which cost consideration is most directly affected?
options: The number of input tokens processed, which increases per-request cost
The number of model layers, which lowers cost
The training dataset license fees
The size of the model checkpoint on disk
explanation: Most foundation model pricing is based on tokens, so larger inputs increase the input token count and therefore the cost of each request.

question: A model evaluation job in Amazon Bedrock reports a low accuracy score on a benchmark task, but human reviewers rate the responses highly for helpfulness. What is the most reasonable conclusion?
options: Automated metrics may not fully capture subjective quality, so both views should be considered
The human reviewers are always wrong
Accuracy is the only metric that matters
The model should be deleted immediately
explanation: Automated metrics and human evaluation measure different aspects of quality; combining them gives a more complete picture of model performance.

question: Which approach generally has the LOWEST upfront cost and effort to customize a model's behavior for a new task?
options: Prompt engineering
Full fine-tuning
Continued pre-training
Training a model from scratch
explanation: Prompt engineering requires no training or weight changes, making it the lowest-cost and fastest way to adapt model behavior.

question: A retailer wants its RAG-based assistant to never discuss competitor pricing and to filter out hateful language. Which Amazon Bedrock feature should be configured?
options: Guardrails with denied topics and content filters
Provisioned Throughput
Model evaluation jobs
Continued pre-training
explanation: Guardrails support denied topics and content filters that can prevent specific subjects and block harmful language in model interactions.

question: Which of the following are examples of business KPIs that could be used to evaluate a deployed generative AI assistant? (Select TWO.)
options: Customer satisfaction score (CSAT)
Reduction in average resolution time
Number of transformer attention heads
Size of the model checkpoint in gigabytes
The model's training learning rate
explanation: Business KPIs such as CSAT and reduced resolution time tie model performance to real organizational outcomes; the other options are internal technical attributes.

question: A company is deciding between two foundation models. Model A is larger, more accurate, and more expensive; Model B is smaller, slightly less accurate, and cheaper. The use case is a real-time chat feature with tight budget limits. What is the best evaluation approach?
options: Weigh accuracy against cost and latency to find the best trade-off for the use case
Always select the most accurate model regardless of cost
Select the model with the largest number of parameters
Choose based solely on the marketing description
explanation: Model selection should balance accuracy, cost, and latency against the specific requirements of the use case rather than optimizing a single dimension.

question: In Amazon Bedrock model evaluation, what is one advantage of using a human-based evaluation job over an automatic one?
options: Humans can assess nuanced qualities like relevance, coherence, and appropriateness
Human evaluation is always faster and cheaper
Human evaluation requires no defined criteria
Human evaluation eliminates the need for test prompts
explanation: Human evaluators can judge subjective and context-dependent qualities that automated metrics struggle to measure accurately.

question: Which of the following best describes the role of a vector embedding in a RAG system?
options: It represents text as numerical vectors so semantically similar content can be retrieved
It permanently updates the foundation model's weights
It encrypts the prompt before sending it to the model
It measures the latency of the inference call
explanation: Embeddings convert text into numeric vectors, enabling similarity search to retrieve the most relevant documents for a query in RAG.

question: A regulated bank needs an assistant grounded in constantly updated policy documents, must cite sources, and cannot risk the model memorizing sensitive data in its weights. Which approach is most appropriate?
options: RAG with a managed knowledge base and citations
Full fine-tuning on the policy documents
Continued pre-training on customer records
Increasing the model temperature to improve grounding
explanation: RAG keeps sensitive, frequently changing data in an external store, supports source citations, and avoids baking confidential data into model weights, which suits regulated grounding requirements.

question: A team fine-tuned a model and saw strong results on their training data but poor results on new, unseen inputs. Which problem does this most likely indicate?
options: Overfitting to the fine-tuning dataset
The model context window being too large
Too few denied topics in Guardrails
Excessive use of RAG retrieval
explanation: Strong performance on training data but weak generalization to new data is a classic sign of overfitting, often caused by too little or unrepresentative training data.

question: An organization wants to reduce per-token inference cost and latency for a fine-tuned model that serves steady, high-volume traffic on Amazon Bedrock. Which option most directly addresses predictable capacity and performance?
options: Provisioned Throughput
On-demand inference only
A larger benchmark dataset
Adding more denied topics to Guardrails
explanation: Provisioned Throughput reserves dedicated model capacity, providing consistent performance for high, predictable workloads, which is required for custom fine-tuned models in many cases.

question: A company combines fine-tuning and RAG for the same application. What is the most accurate rationale for using both together?
options: Fine-tuning shapes the model's behavior and style while RAG supplies current, factual knowledge
RAG retrains the weights and fine-tuning fetches documents
Both techniques serve the identical purpose, so redundancy improves accuracy
Using both removes the need to evaluate the model
explanation: Fine-tuning is best for behavior, tone, and task format, while RAG is best for injecting up-to-date factual context; combining them leverages each technique's strength.

question: Which of the following are valid reasons to choose RAG instead of fine-tuning for a use case? (Select TWO.)
options: The underlying knowledge changes frequently and must stay current
You need answers grounded in private documents without altering model weights
You want to permanently change the model's writing style
You want to reduce the model's parameter count
You have no source documents at all
explanation: RAG excels when knowledge changes often and when grounding answers in private data without modifying the model is required; style changes are better suited to fine-tuning.

question: Which factors are important trade-offs to consider when selecting a foundation model for a production application? (Select THREE.)
options: Inference cost
Response latency
Accuracy or quality on the target task
The model author's nationality
The color of the AWS console
explanation: Cost, latency, and task accuracy or quality are core trade-offs in model selection, while the other options are irrelevant to performance or value.
